title: Relaunch intro: Quietly building, now sharing
caption:
Quietly building. Now sharing. 🌱

For a while, Build & Bloom Collective has been doing the work behind the scenes: strategy, operations, workshops, and events alongside helping organizations, founders, nonprofits, and community teams.

Now we're opening the door so you can see it.

Here you'll find:
• Ways to build work that doesn't burn people out
• Psychology-informed leadership and team wellness
• Tools for your own growth, faith, and rest

Rooted in justice, collective care, and intentional growth. Tell me below: what are you building right now?

title: Value card: Infrastructure is care
caption:
Infrastructure is care.

We usually talk about burnout as a personal problem: rest more, set boundaries, take a vacation. Those matter.

But how work is built shapes how people feel inside it. Clear roles, steady rhythms, and simple systems protect people before they're running on empty. That's the heart of organizational wellness.

Which does your team need most right now: clearer roles, better rhythms, or simpler systems? Tell me below.

title: You're not lazy. You're stuck in trying.
caption:
You're not lazy. You're stuck in trying.

I lived there for a long time: busy but not moving, planning instead of starting, pouring into everyone else, and quietly doubting what I already knew I was called to do.

Trying is comfortable because it keeps one foot out the door. Doing puts both feet in.

Which of these six sounds most like you right now? Tell me the number in the comments. 👇

All it takes is the right yes to go from trying to doing. My new 21-day guide, The Right Yes, arrives Friday.

title: LAUNCH: The Right Yes is here
caption:
It's here. 🌱

The Right Yes is a 21-day guide from trying to doing. I wrote it for the season I was in for too long: busy but not moving, planning for years, carrying everyone else, and hearing God clearly without moving.

Inside:
• Week 1, Hear It: get honest about where you've been circling
• Week 2, Clear It: practice the no's that make room
• Week 3, Say It: recognize your right yes and put it in motion

Every day takes about 15 minutes: a short reading, scripture and reflection, a journal prompt, and one small Right Yes step.

It's a digital download you can read on your phone or print as a workbook.

All it takes is the right yes to go from trying to doing. Link in bio.

title: A no is a complete sentence.
caption:
A no is a complete sentence. 🤍

For years I over-explained every no: long messages, extra apologies, a paragraph of reasons. It left me exhausted and still feeling guilty.

Here's what I learned. Every yes is also a no to something else. The no is happening either way. The only question is whether you're choosing it on purpose.

Save these four scripts for the next time someone asks for more than you have room for. Share this with the friend who needs it.

From Day 14 of The Right Yes. Link in bio.

title: How do you know it's the right yes?
caption:
"How do I know it's the right yes?"

It's the question I hear most. Not every good idea is your idea. Not every open door is your door.

The right yes usually has most of these six marks. And notice what isn't on the list: certainty, perfect timing, or everyone's approval. Those rarely come first.

What's the yes that keeps coming back to you? You don't have to share it here. Just name it to yourself today.

Day 15 of The Right Yes goes deeper. Link in bio.
